issues.legal_issue: A litigant asserting individual land rights cannot rely on an unraised claim concerning another person's mineral title to invalidate state action.
material_facts: The appellant's writ petition included an averment that some land remained subject to the former zamindars' rights because the abolition law had not been extended to it.
The argument that the former zamindars retained mineral rights was not made before either court in the High Court.
The appellant brought the writ petition to assert his own rights, while the claim about mineral title concerned the former zamindars and the State.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the argument because it had not been argued in the High Court and concerned rights the appellant could not assert on behalf of others.
issues.legal_principle: An appellate court will not entertain an argument that was not advanced in the courts below; a party seeking to vindicate individual rights cannot obtain relief by asserting that state action prejudices another person's rights. The Court applied this principle in reviewing the High Court's dismissal of a writ petition under Article 226.

predicates.appeal_from_individual_rights_writ: The proceeding is an appeal from the dismissal of a writ petition brought to assert the appellant's individual rights.
predicates.issue_not_urged_below: The appellant did not advance the argument in the courts below.
predicates.claim_concerns_another_persons_rights: The argument relies on rights belonging to someone other than the appellant.

issues.definition: When an appeal from an individual-rights writ raises an argument not advanced below that concerns another person's rights, the argument is not entertained.

issues.legal_issue: A riparian landholder does not acquire a superior right to river-borne minor minerals deposited on the land, and the State may regulate their extraction.
material_facts: Floodwaters carried sand, gravel, stones and bajri from the river onto land abutting the river.
The State had title to the deposits while they were in the river, and the former zamindars' rights to mines and minerals had vested in the State under the land abolition law.
The deposits were ordinary sand, gravel, building stones and bajri, which fell within the defined category of minor minerals.
The State proposed to auction the right to remove the deposits, and the appellant sought to prevent the auction.
issues.conclusion: The deposits were minor minerals subject to state regulation, and the appellant could not extract them without a lease or permit from the State; the river's movement of the deposits onto private land did not defeat the State's title.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(e) of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, and Rules 2(7) and 3 of the Uttar Pradesh Minor Minerals (Concession) Rules, 1963, cover the specified deposits and require mining operations to be conducted under a lease or permit. Sections 4 and 6(a)(i) and (ii) of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1951, vested the intermediaries' rights, including rights to mines and minerals, in the State. The Court approved Sultan v. State of U.P.; it also relied on Halsbury's Laws of England on ownership of river and seabed materials and on Norman S. Wear v. State of Kansas concerning migratory riverbed sand.

rule.if: challenge_to_state_mining_auction and river_flood_moved_minerals_to_private_land and minerals_fit_regulated_category and (state_owned_minerals_before_movement or former_mineral_rights_transferred_to_state)

predicates.challenge_to_state_mining_auction: The proceeding challenges a state auction of the right to remove minerals.
predicates.river_flood_moved_minerals_to_private_la: Floodwaters carried minerals from a river onto privately held or used land beside the river.
predicates.minerals_fit_regulated_category: The deposited materials are of a kind that falls within the legally defined category of regulated minor minerals.
predicates.state_owned_minerals_before_movement: The State owned the minerals while they were in the river.
predicates.former_mineral_rights_transferred_to_sta: A law transferred the former landholders' rights to mines and minerals to the State.

issues.definition: When a challenge to a state mining auction concerns regulated minerals moved by a river onto private land, and the State owned them before movement or received the former mineral rights, the State may control their extraction.

issues.legal_issue: Minerals need not be beneath the soil, and removing surface deposits to obtain them constitutes a mining operation.
material_facts: The sand, gravel and other materials were deposited on the surface of the land rather than beneath it.
The proposed activity involved removing or collecting those materials to obtain the minerals.
issues.conclusion: The surface location of the deposits did not prevent them from being minerals, and removing them to obtain them constituted a mining operation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(d) and 3(e) of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, and Rules 2(5) and 2(7) of the Uttar Pradesh Minor Minerals (Concession) Rules, 1963, do not require minerals to be subterranean. The Court construed “winning” a mineral to include extracting or otherwise obtaining it.

predicates.challenge_to_mining_regulation: The proceeding challenges the application of mining regulation to the removal of materials.
predicates.minerals_are_on_land_surface: The minerals are deposited on the surface of land rather than beneath it.
predicates.removal_activity_obtains_minerals: A person proposes to remove or collect the materials in order to obtain the minerals.

issues.definition: If a challenge to mining regulation concerns surface minerals and an activity that obtains them by removal, that activity is a mining operation.

issues.legal_issue: A person entitled to use land is entitled to compensation when mining activity under a lease or permit deprives that person of the land's use.
material_facts: The State's proposed mining activity could prevent the person entitled to use the land from using it, including for agriculture.
The State accepted that compensation was payable for deprivation of land use and that a District Officer would determine the amount if the parties disputed it.
issues.conclusion: The person entitled to use the land is entitled to compensation for deprivation caused by mining activity, and the District Officer determining disputed compensation should consider all relevant factors, particularly the duration of the deprivation.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 67 of the Uttar Pradesh Minor Minerals (Concession) Rules, 1963, entitles a person having a right in any capacity in land covered by a mining lease or permit to compensation for use of the surface; the amount may be agreed by the parties or determined by the District Officer in the event of dispute. The Court noted the State's concession and stated that the duration of deprivation was a particularly relevant factor.

predicates.mining_authorization_covers_land_used_by: A mining lease or permit covers land that another person is entitled to use.
predicates.mining_activity_deprives_land_user_of_us: The mining activity prevents or limits that person's use of the land.
predicates.person_has_right_to_use_land: The person deprived of use has a right in some capacity to use the land.

issues.definition: When authorized mining on land deprives a person with a right to use that land of its use, that person is entitled to compensation.
